name: Harvey
bestFor: The category-leading AI platform for law firms and in-house legal teams doing document-heavy legal work
description: A legal AI platform built with and for law firms, handling contract analysis, research, drafting, and due diligence at the level of accuracy large firms require, deeply integrated into legal workflows.

freeTier.limits: No free tier; enterprise sales process only

paidTier.notes: No published pricing. Industry-reported figures: roughly $1,000–$2,000/user/month for mid-market firms, dropping to $100–$200/user/month at Am Law 100 scale with volume discounts; 25–50 seat minimums; median annual contract reported around $175,000 — not official figures.

name: Ironclad (Jurist AI)
bestFor: AI-assisted contract lifecycle management — drafting, redlining, and analyzing contracts at scale
description: A contract lifecycle management platform whose Jurist AI Assist and AI Contract Analysis modules draft, review, and extract obligations from contracts, integrated into approval workflows.

freeTier.limits: No free tier; demo-and-quote sales process

paidTier.notes: No published pricing. Reported figures: base platform roughly $30,000–$250,000+/year (mid-market commonly $50K–$120K); the Jurist AI Assist add-on is separately reported at $50,000–$200,000/year — not official figures.

name: Spellbook
bestFor: AI contract drafting and redlining that works inside Microsoft Word, for smaller legal teams
description: An AI contract-drafting copilot that runs as a Word add-in, suggesting redlines, flagging risky clauses, and drafting new provisions in the tool lawyers already draft in.

freeTier.limits: 7-day free trial (extended trials for larger organizations); no persistent free tier

paidTier.notes: No published price list — priced by the number of team members on a license, via demo. Industry-reported figures: Associate-level plans around $89/user/month, rising to Enterprise reported around $350/user/month with a 6-month minimum commitment — not official figures.

name: CoCounsel (Thomson Reuters)
bestFor: AI legal research, drafting, and document review for firms already on Westlaw or Practical Law
description: Thomson Reuters' AI legal assistant, uniting research, drafting, and document analysis in one experience and grounded in Westlaw and Practical Law's trusted content — priced through a self-serve configurator for small firms or sales quote for larger ones.

freeTier.limits: Free trial available on CoCounsel Essentials; no persistent free tier

paidTier.notes: Self-serve configurator (firms up to 10 attorneys) prices CoCounsel Essentials around $293/user and CoCounsel Legal around $492/user (annual terms); reported figures elsewhere cite CoCounsel Core from roughly $4,500/user/year rising to ~$9,000/user/year bundled with Westlaw. Firms over 10 attorneys are quoted by sales — not official list prices.

name: LegalOn
bestFor: AI contract review against expert-built playbooks, scaled from solo attorneys to full in-house legal teams
description: An AI contract review and drafting platform that checks contracts against expert-built playbooks and flags risky clauses, for solo attorneys, fractional GCs, and in-house legal teams.

freeTier.limits: Demo available on request; no persistent free tier

paidTier.notes: The previously published self-serve 'Individual' plan ($550/month, unlimited reviews) is no longer listed. LegalOn now shows three quote-only tiers scaled to team size — Core Review (solo attorneys/fractional GCs), Contracting Suite (in-house teams), and Productivity Suite (full legal workday) — with no public per-seat price; a demo/sales conversation is required for all of them.
